aab3c8c42c:
This capstone builds the exam's Multi-Agent Research System scenario. A coordinator agent receives a research question. It delegates to specialised subagents (web search, document analysis, synthesis, report generation) and produces a cited report.

The official sample questions from this scenario are some of the most instructive in the guide.

One describes a report on "the impact of AI on creative industries" that covers only visual arts, even though every subagent succeeded. The root cause is the coordinator's decomposition.

Another asks how a subagent should report a timeout. The answer is structured error context with the attempted query and partial results. Not a generic "search unavailable", and not an empty success.
301fe26082:
Chapter 2 explained the theory: hub-and-spoke topology, isolated subagent context, the Task tool and AgentDefinition, self-contained Task prompts, a hand-rolled coordinator, and session forking. This chapter doesn't re-teach those.

Instead it builds one codebase that exercises all of them at once, with two implementations of the same design. One is a plain Messages-API orchestrator where your code owns the loop. The other is an Agent SDK configuration where the SDK owns it.

Both run offline against a local corpus and a deterministic mock model. So every acceptance test runs in CI without a key.
b59af64834:
Write the requirements as you would for any distributed workflow. Separate what must hold on every run from what depends on model judgement.

In a research system, the invariants are about honesty of the output: no claim without a source, no silent loss of a subtopic, no number that quietly replaces another. Judgement covers what to research and how to phrase the narrative.
97d8a197bf:
The key design choice is where the line falls between code and model in synthesis.

Ask a model to "merge these findings and keep citations" and it usually will. The exam scenario is built on the cases where it doesn't: a summarisation step drops attributions, or two percentages become one.

So the merge is deterministic. Findings arrive as structured objects. Code groups them, detects conflicts by metric key, assigns claim ids and builds the coverage table. The model writes prose that refers to C07, and the renderer attaches the sources.

It's the same split as keeping money arithmetic out of a template engine.
45f87430db:
The figure is the Chapter 2 topology made concrete. Note three choices.

  • The researchers run on Haiku 4.5 (claude-haiku-4-5), because each does a narrow extraction many times in parallel. The coordinator decides scope and recovery, so it runs on Sonnet 5.5.
  • The doc-analyst is a separate role because internal documents need different tools (file read, grep). They also need a different prompt: note the methodology, such as sample weighting, that explains a number.
  • The synthesizer has neither WebSearch nor Task. If it finds a doubtful claim, it may check that one quote against the cited source, and nothing more.
3abaaa7f84:
A fake search backend is only useful if its data contains the situations the system must handle.

The corpus has fifteen web pages across five creative areas (visual arts, music, writing, film, games) and three internal documents. Each page is markdown with front matter and a "Key findings" list. Quantitative findings carry a machine tag with a stable metric key. That's how the merge recognises two sources talking about the same number.
4d709988c5:
Two conflicts are planted on purpose.

  • The music share is 18% in an April article and 28% in a September one. That's a change over time.
  • The games figure is 62% in an open developer survey and 31% in an internal weighted panel. That's a difference in method: a self-selected versus a reweighted sample.

A good report shows both pairs and says which kind of difference each might be. It doesn't pick one.

The internal documents also give the system somewhere to go when web search fails. That's what makes the recovery path testable.
80e160837b:
CorpusTools stands in for WebSearch, WebFetch and Read. Search scores pages by token overlap, with a boost for the area name.

A FaultPlan injects the failures the tests need:

  • transient 503s for a given query (recoverable);
  • a kill switch after N searches (access failure for the rest of the run);
  • a per-call delay, to make parallelism measurable.
94ddf621d8:
The two exception classes encode the distinction task 5.3 cares about.

A transient error is the subagent's problem. Retry it locally, and don't bother the coordinator.

An unavailable service is the coordinator's problem. Only the coordinator can decide whether to wait, switch to another agent, or report a gap.
e26417b259:
Everything that crosses an agent boundary is a Pydantic model. Free text never crosses alone.

This is the single most important decision in the codebase. Provenance (5.6) and error propagation (5.3) are both properties of the data that moves between agents. You can't recover a field that was never sent.
140e5ea88e:
The validator makes it impossible to blur access failure with a valid empty result.

  • empty means the searches ran and found nothing in scope. It must not carry a failure type.
  • failed means the work couldn't be done. It must say why.
  • partial means some findings exist and something went wrong.

That last one is the shape of the official sample answer: the failure type, the attempted query, partial results and potential alternatives.
67467bcd0c: The report schema has its own integrity check. Every claim id a section cites must exist. Every claim marked contested must belong to a Conflict with at least two values. So a synthesizer output that references C99 fails validation, instead of rendering a dangling citation.
6a85dbf930:
Every model call in the Messages-API version goes through one method: complete_json(role, system, user, schema, model).

The live implementation forces a tool call whose input_schema is the expected schema. So the reply is always JSON of the right shape. This is the structured-output technique from Domain 4, used here as plumbing.
14fb0f12e0:
MockLLM is a test double, not a model. It reads the same system prompt and payload, and applies rules that imitate the behaviour the tests care about.

The rule that matters most: if the coordinator prompt asks the model to list every sub-area, it returns five subtopics. Otherwise it returns two subtopics about the most salient angle, AI art.

That's how a real model tends to fail with a vague prompt. The mock reproduces it deterministically, so you can write a test for it.
480bbe0640:
Keeping the mock honest matters. It extracts findings only from sources it was given. It copies quotes verbatim. It skips URLs listed in already_found, and it skips off-scope sources.

If the mock cheated (say, by returning findings for areas it was never sent), tests would pass for the wrong reason. A quick check: swap in AnthropicLLM. The same tests should still describe what you expect, only with variance.
423611c69f:
The narrow-decomposition sample question is answered by changing the coordinator prompt, not the subagents. The good prompt makes breadth an explicit step and adds a self-check.

The bad prompt stays in the repository as a fixture, so the failure can be reproduced on demand. It's the same reason you keep a known-bad input in a regression suite.
c69ca64aa8:
Step 3 of the good prompt also handles the duplication problem from task 1.2. Scope boundaries ("Music production and streaming only. Not in scope: Visual arts..., Writing..., Film..., Video games") stop two researchers from returning the same article.

The researcher prompt enforces the other half. Stay inside the assigned scope, and don't repeat anything listed under already_found.
e49f9ec093:
A subagent is an async function from a SubagentTask to a SubagentResult. The task is its entire world: subtopic, scope, queries, document paths and the URLs already found.

There's no shared state object and no access to the coordinator's history. This is isolated context (Chapter 2, section 3), expressed as a function signature.
098fd9ac88:
The web researcher runs its queries, fetches the hits, and asks the model to extract findings. Then it checks every finding against what it actually read.

A finding is dropped if it cites a URL the subagent never fetched, or quotes text that doesn't appear in the source. The check is cheap and deterministic. It catches the most damaging hallucination in research systems: a plausible quote attached to a real URL.
062903ba44: The end of web_researcher is where task 5.3 lives. It distinguishes three outcomes, and each produces a different, valid SubagentResult.
0b4936681f:
Compare this with the two wrong answers from the sample question.

A generic {"error": "search unavailable"} hides what was attempted and what was already retrieved. The coordinator can't choose between retrying, switching agents or reporting a gap.

Returning {"findings": []} as success is worse. The synthesizer will write "no evidence was found about music". That's a false statement about the world, caused by an outage.

The structured result keeps the findings that did arrive (partial). It names the failed query, lists what was retrieved before the failure, and offers alternatives.
e03cbfed1b: Finally, a boundary wrapper guarantees that no exception escapes a subagent. Maybe the model call raises, or the code has a bug. Either way, the coordinator still receives a SubagentResult with failure_type=internal and the exception text in the coverage note. One subagent crashing never takes down the gather.
b76dee8e3a: The Messages-API coordinator is a plain class. Its run method is the whole lifecycle in eleven lines. Every arrow in the hub-and-spoke diagram corresponds to a line here.
73f1a1886d:
Two details carry exam weight.

First, delegate spawns all tasks of a round in one asyncio.gather. That's the code equivalent of the coordinator emitting several Task tool calls in a single response, which task 1.3 names as the way to run subagents in parallel. Spawning them one per turn would serialise the work for no reason.

Second, the loop is bounded twice. max_rounds caps refinement. And the gap evaluator refuses to re-delegate a subtopic that has failed twice. Without that second bound, a dead search service produces an infinite retry loop that looks like diligence.
6b4cffd145:
Gap evaluation is a model call. Deciding whether coverage is sufficient, and which agent to try next, is judgement.

But the input to that call is a compact, structured summary built by code, not the raw subagent outputs. The coordinator sees counts, statuses, failure types and alternatives. It doesn't need the full text of fifteen articles to decide that music has only one source.
572d1bf353:
Re-delegation passes prior work explicitly. A re-delegated researcher receives already_found, the URLs that earlier rounds already turned into findings, because it has no memory of them.

This is Chapter 2's point about context passing, applied to iteration. The second round is a new agent with a new context. Anything it should know must be in the brief.
3a468dd855:
Synthesis has two halves.

The deterministic half is merge_findings. It turns all findings from all rounds into numbered claims, each with a list of SourceRefs. It deduplicates numbers by metric and value, and everything else by normalised text.

When two sources report the same metric with different values, it marks both claims contested. It then builds a Conflict that lists every value with its source and date, sorted by date.
e414275315:
Why sort by date, and mention it in the annotation? Task 5.6 asks for publication dates so a reader can tell a temporal difference from a contradiction.

18% in April and 28% in September is consistent with growth. 62% in an open survey and 31% in a weighted panel is a methodological difference.

The system doesn't decide which is which. It gives the reader what they need to decide. The doc-analyst prompt asks for methodology notes, so the panel finding carries "weighted panel, not self-selected" with it.
3b3c751cc5:
The model half is small on purpose. Per section, the synthesizer receives the claim ids, texts and statuses. It returns a summary plus the claim ids it relies on. It's told not to add facts, numbers or sources, and to name both values of a contested claim.

build_report then filters out any claim id or subtopic id the model made up. Pydantic validates the whole Report.
81645d6fe8:
The coverage table is built from the same history:

  • a subtopic with findings and no failures is covered;
  • with findings and at least one failure, it's partial;
  • with no findings, it's not_covered.

The note column says which agent failed, how, on which query, and how many results came back before the failure. It also records valid-empty results separately. A reader can tell "nothing exists" from "we could not look".
99ceee766c:
In the SDK version, you don't write the loop. The coordinator is the main agent. It spawns subagents by calling the Task tool. The SDK runs each subagent in a fresh context and returns its final message as the Task tool result.

Your job shrinks to configuration: the coordinator's prompt and allowed_tools, plus one AgentDefinition per role. Each definition has a description (the coordinator routes on it), a prompt, a tool list and a model.
c6eb062ce8:
The configuration is first written as plain data and validated in pure Python. That keeps the rules testable without the SDK installed.

It also puts the most common misconfiguration, a coordinator without "Task", behind an exception. Otherwise you'd get a confusing run where the coordinator tries to do the research itself.
61f37ae642:
The synthesizer's one tool is an in-process MCP server built with @tool and create_sdk_mcp_server.

This is the task 2.3 pattern for "a role occasionally needs a capability from another role". Give it a narrow tool for the frequent case: check one quote against one cited source. Route anything larger back through the coordinator.

Giving the synthesizer WebSearch would let it start new research mid-synthesis. That mixes roles and bypasses the coordinator's coverage tracking.
49f2f1b18b:
Every claude_agent_sdk import sits inside a function. So the package imports, and the offline tests run, on a machine without the SDK. The one test that builds real ClaudeAgentOptions is skipped when the SDK is missing.

The mcp__research__verify_fact name follows the SDK's mcp__<server>__<tool> convention for MCP tools.
7a3f00a22b:
Research runs are long. The two session operations from task 1.7 map to two real needs.

Resume continues a session with its history. Use it after an interrupted run, or when the user asks a follow-up about one subtopic.

Fork branches a new session from an existing one: same history up to that point, new session id, original untouched. It fits "try a different synthesis without paying for the research again".
f2802265c7:
A caution the exam tests: resuming is right only when the earlier context is still valid.

If the corpus or the sites changed since the session ran, a resumed coordinator reasons over stale tool results it believes are current. In that case, start a fresh session and pass a structured summary of prior findings (with their dates) in the first message. Or tell the resumed session explicitly which sources changed.
2c7c0a8f4a:
Look at that output carefully. It's the sample question in miniature.

Every subtopic is covered. No subagent failed. There are no conflicts. And the report misses music, writing, film and games.

Nothing in the coverage table can detect this, because the table only measures the plan against itself. The test has to compare the plan against the question's scope. That's why test_decomposition_covers_all_five_areas asserts on the set of areas.
2efe06d8bf: Twenty tests run in about three seconds, with no network. They're organised by task statement. Each one asserts on an outcome a reviewer could check by hand.
44ae3f5b0d:
The other tests cover:

  • parallelism: with a 50 ms delay per search, the run must finish well under the sequential time, and the first batch must contain all five researchers;
  • explicit context: every extract call payload has exactly subtopic, already_found and sources;
  • local retry of transient errors: two 503s, then success, and the coordinator sees success;
  • the boundary wrapper: a model exception becomes failure_type=internal;
  • the schema validators;
  • invented quotes: a lying extractor yields zero claims and every row not_covered, rather than a confident report built on fabricated quotes.
56a9d43c31:
The CLI runs offline against a 15-page fake web corpus and three internal documents, with a deterministic mock in place of the model.

Three runs of the question "Impact of AI on creative industries" show the system in its normal, degraded and defective modes. The outputs below are captured from real runs.
76d5376708: Five areas, all covered, 22 claims, two conflicts. Each section of the report lists claims with a link and a publication date. Claims whose figure has a counterpart in another source carry a [CONTESTED] tag. The report ends with a "Conflicting figures" section that shows each pair side by side:
3437e63241:
The two figures aren't an error. They're five months apart, and the later source is the one titled "over a quarter". A reader who sees only 28% wouldn't know the earlier measurement existed. One who sees only 18% would underestimate.

The same section handles the second conflict: a 62 percent studio-adoption figure from a developer survey, against 31 percent from a weighted panel. A weighted panel and a self-selected survey measure different things. That's why the claim record has method and population fields (Chapter 16).
7568a2c198:
The run doesn't crash, and it doesn't pretend.

Four areas are partial, each with the failed query and how many results arrived before the failure. The report has a Coverage table (subtopic, status, findings, sources, attempts, note) and a Known gaps list.

The attempts column shows 2 for the four failing areas and 1 for the one that finished before the kill switch. Here's what happened. The coordinator evaluated coverage and re-delegated once, with already_found and a narrower task. The second attempt hit the same dead tool. The gap was reported instead of looped on.

Notice too that music, film and games still show findings from internal documents. The document analyst doesn't use the search tool. So the outage degraded one path and not the other, which is exactly what an alternative source in the error payload is for (Chapter 15). Writing and publishing has no internal document, so it's partial on web results alone.

The claim count stays 22 here because the corpus is small and the kill comes late in the run. Don't read it as a general property.
a2adbe560b:
This is the exam's scenario, reproduced.

With the narrow coordinator prompt, the plan has two subtopics, both about visual arts. Every subagent succeeds. Coverage reads covered twice. The report is confident, well cited, and wrong about the question, because it never mentions music, writing, film or games. Eight claims instead of 22. No conflicts found, because the conflicting sources were never searched.

There's no error to catch. The failure is in the plan, and the only defence is to check the decomposition against the question. Here, that's the test test_narrow_prompt_reproduces_too_narrow_decomposition and its good-prompt twin, test_decomposition_covers_all_five_areas.

The official sample answer for this scenario names the coordinator's decomposition as the root cause. The log, the subagent outputs and the coverage table all look healthy.
3c76021403:
Two of these deserve singling out.

test_result_schema_rejects_inconsistent_status exists because certain combinations are the signature of code that lost the distinction between failure and success. A status of ok with a non-empty failure list is one. failed with findings and no failure is another. The validator makes both unrepresentable at the boundary.

test_invented_quote_is_dropped feeds the merge a claim whose quote doesn't occur in the fetched source. It asserts that the claim disappears from the report. It's the executable form of "provenance is a property you check, not a thing you ask for".

The cost is the one noted in the table. A model that paraphrases a quote loses a true claim. That's why the subagent prompt asks for verbatim quotes.
dbc75821a3:
Treat each report as a data product with its own quality numbers.

  • Track coverage by area per report (share covered, partial, not_covered). Alert when the partial share rises after a provider change.
  • Track subagent failures by type and by tool. A rise in rate_limited means you should lower concurrency. A rise in permission_denied means a credential expired.
  • Track decomposition quality directly. Sample reports, have a person list the areas the question needed, and compare with the plan. That's the only metric that sees run 3.
  • Track conflict counts. Zero conflicts across many sources may mean the merge key is too strict. Dozens may mean it's too loose.

Keep the claim records, not only the rendered report. They're what lets a person audit a number a month later.
c59e988ead:
Cost control follows from the structure. Subagent work is parallel, and it's the largest part of the bill. So:

  • size the model per role (a smaller model for fetch-and-extract and a larger one for synthesis is a common split, to be confirmed by your own evals);
  • cap re-delegation at one round;
  • give each subagent a token budget.

The coordinator's context stays small because it receives claim records, not page text. It's the same argument as Chapter 14's case-facts block.
32b888bcb6:
The Messages API version maps onto a service with a bounded executor. The coordinator is a method that builds a plan, submits one task per subtopic and joins the results.

Each subagent is a function that returns a sealed result type. Success and failure are both values, and the compiler forces the caller to handle each.
844fcbde0a: The type system does the work the Python validator does. A switch over a sealed interface has to name every case, so nobody can add a new status without the coverage code noticing. Virtual threads make the parallel gather cheap, and a semaphore bounds concurrency against the provider's rate limit.
8a891b880a: Add a sixth area (architecture and design) with a conflicting figure in the corpus. The conflict should appear in the report with no change to synthesis.py. If it doesn't, what does that tell you about the merge key?
59bbc539da: Add a per-subagent timeout that maps to FailureType.TIMEOUT and keeps partial results. What does the coordinator do differently for a timeout than for a 403?
d9a6a28d96: Write a decomposition check. It compares the plan with a list of required areas supplied by a person. If one is missing, it fails the run before any subagent starts.
f2cb0bf60e: Add a PostToolUse hook in the SDK version that rejects a subagent result missing source_url and returns a corrective message. How do you avoid an infinite correction loop?
c595077709:
Situation. The research system has run in production for a month. A reviewer reports three problems:

  • A report on "AI in the telecom sector" covered network operations and customer care, but not fraud, billing or field service.
  • A report stated "62% of game studios use generative AI", while the internal panel said 31%.
  • On a day the search provider had an outage, a report said "no published evidence was found on AI in film".

Which changes, in what order?
d8947f642f: Classify. The film statement is false information produced by an outage. An output-honesty invariant is broken. The 62% claim lost a competing figure, which breaks a provenance invariant. The telecom coverage is a decomposition judgement problem.
7201efd345: Fix the outage path first. Find where "no results" and "search down" are merged. In this codebase, that would be a subagent returning status="empty" on ToolUnavailable. Make it return failed/partial with access_failure, the attempted query and alternatives. Add the schema validator, and make the report list the subtopic under Known gaps. Reject "retry until it works": it's unbounded, and still silent when it gives up.
aac285702b: Then provenance. Check whether the merge is done by code or by a model. If a model merges, it can pick one number. Move the claim-source map and conflict detection into code keyed by metric. Have the doc-analyst record methodology, so the 31% panel figure carries "weighted, not self-selected". Reject "tell the synthesizer to keep both numbers" as the only fix. It lowers the rate; it doesn't remove it.
f16ab216be: Then decomposition. Change the coordinator prompt to enumerate sub-areas and self-check. Keep the old prompt as a regression fixture. Add an eval that asserts on the set of areas for a handful of broad questions. Reject "add more researchers" and "use a larger model for researchers": the missing areas were never assigned.
8d953bafb3: Create a venv, run pip install -r requirements.txt, then run pytest -q. Done when 20 tests pass with no API key (one is skipped if claude-agent-sdk isn't installed).
e5571cca70: Run python run.py --kill-search-after 6 and read out/trace.txt. Done when you can point to the batch of 8, the re-delegation line, and the cap that stops round 3.
934f5b9fc2: Add a sixth area with one conflicting figure to corpus/web, and extend AREAS and the mock labels. Done when the conflict appears in the report with no change to synthesis.py.
6a378451e0: With a key, run --sdk. Then run --sdk --resume <id> --fork with a different synthesis request. Done when the fork has a new session id, and a rerun of the original id still shows the first synthesis.
